column1: # Shared rows for a fork layer's 1.21.5 target (and every later one that inherits it).
# 1.21.5 is where CompoundTag/ListTag getters started returning Optional -- the same change 26.2 carries
# ⚠ NOT copied verbatim: the 26.2 rows matched `.getInt(<anything without a comma>)`, which also rewrites a
# ByteBuffer read (`bytes.getInt(at)` -> `bytes.getIntOr(at, 0)`) -- Battle of Lord had no binary readers, the
# first fork that went through here (a Blender/glTF loader) has eight. A shared row cannot know the receiver's
# type, so it anchors on what the NBT API guarantees and a byte offset never is: a string literal key, or an
# UPPER_CASE constant (bare or Class.CONST). A key held in a variable, and a ListTag index, are left to the
# fork's own rows or its workers.
#!exhaustive  # shared library: most forks use only some of these rows
# CompoundTag.getUUID/putUUID/hasUUID are gone; a UUID goes through UUIDUtil.CODEC (the same int[4] on disk).
# Each needs an argument, so the many no-arg Entity.getUUID() calls are untouched.
# CompoundTag.contains(key, type) lost its type argument (from the 26.2 table, verbatim: anchored on a tag id).
